It's really hard to explain this kind of stuff in any detail over a comments thread. The physics background you get in either highschool physics or most undergraduate physics courses is such a glossing over of physics concepts that it may as well be a lie.

Electromagnetic waves have two components - electrical fields and magnetic fields. They also have a defining frequency. The way an EM wave interacts with a material is highly based on its frequency - many things that are good shields at a certain frequency are poor shields at others. Metals tend to block out the electrical component of waves, but nothing blocks magnetic fields. However, some materials are more "permeable" to magnetic fields than others, meaning that the magnetic field preferentially travel through that material instead of going into the thing you are trying to shield from magnetic fields. Unalloyed iron is good for this. Think of it like a flood bearing down on your house - you won't stop it, but you can dig a channel around your house that the water can flow through more easily. This is also related to the whole "EMP shielding" thing talked about in prepper circles - it's a very complex topic.
